None of these can run arbitrary system commands like modifying `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward`.

If you want to enable IP forwarding on a Linux system, you'd need to run this yourself in a terminal with appropriate privileges:

```bash
sudo sh -c 'echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward'
```

Or, equivalently:

```bash
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
```

To make it persistent across reboots, add `net.ipv4.ip_forward=1` to `/etc/sysctl.conf` (or a file in `/etc/sysctl.d/`) and run `sudo sysctl -p`.
